recipes.name: Mexican Pasta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained
1 (11 ounce) can canned whole-kernel corn with red and green bell peppers
1 (4.25 ounce) can sliced black olives, drained
0.5 teaspoon ground cumin, or to taste
0.5 teaspoon dried cilantro, or to taste

steps.text: Bring a large pot with lightly salted water to a rolling boil. Stir in pasta and return to a boil. Cook pasta uncovered, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes.

While pasta is cooking, combine salsa, mayonnaise, sour cream, and bell pepper in a large bowl. Add black beans, corn, olives, green onions, salt, garlic powder, cumin, cilantro, and pepper; stir until well combined.
Drain pasta. Rinse under cold running water until completely cooled; drain thoroughly.
Add cooled pasta to salsa and vegetable mixture; stir until evenly coated. For best results, cover salad with plastic wrap and refrigerate until chilled before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Mexican Pasta Salad
raw_recipe.description: This creamy Mexican pasta salad with rotini pasta, salsa, black beans, corn, and bell pepper, makes a zingy change from traditional pasta salads.

review.reviewBody: Wow this was fantastic! I made it for a BBQ last night as I thought it would be something unexpected and less likely to be duplicated. I was right! I like to make a new recipe exactly as it's written to give an accurate review, but I did use fat free sour cream and light mayo (I'm trying to drop a few pounds) and it was so creamy you wouldn't have guessed it was healthy. There was just the right amount of wet ingredients so it wasn't dry and there were so many textures with the olives and corn and beans! My taste test turned into a bowl of it before the BBQ and everyone raved about it. I am making this again next week for another BBQ and I will try not to eat it all before hand! Thanks so much for the recipe!

I just made this for Memorial Day party. I wanted it to be more like a meal so I added diced cooked chicken and cheese chunks. I also used diced fresh garlic and diced fresh cilantro instead of dry. One last alteration I did was add fresh squeezed lime and lemon juice to add extra freshness. It's amazing!

Good. I had some leftover, slow cooked taco chicken made earlier this week (plus reserved juices/sauce) so I added that and in turn, cut the salsa down by half. Followed the rest per recipe. Letting it sit a few hours at minimum to “set-up” really is necessary. My husband and I shared a bowl immediately and we found only okay. Tried a few hours later - agreed we liked. Makes a lot so maybe overnight, I might find this outstanding!? Good easy recipe - and in my case; happy to use up leftovers! Thank you!
left out olives, used vegan mayo (chipole flavor), vegan sour cream, used navy beans along with the black beans ( half can black beans and half can navy beans) was used in recipe.

I love this recipe! I have made it several times, and it is my new favorite pasta salad. I do make a few changes: (1) I leave out the sweet peppers, just for preference. (2) I do one can of plain, regular sweet corn or a cup of frozen corn instead of corn with peppers. (3) I dice a couple of sweet onion slices instead of the green onions (4) I replace the cilantro with parsley. I personally like eating the salad right after I make it, but it's delicious after a few hours, as well. The first time I made it, I put in round 2 pounds of cooked ground beef and it was really good, but I would just recommend maybe making a little more of the salsa, mayo, and sour cream sauce for adding that much meat.

Not sure what some of these reviewers think they wanted, but this was a lovely recipe. Rich, creamy, cool, fresh, and flavorful - not full of heat, but you could bump that up easily if you wanted to. I didn't have Mexican corn on hand, but I used a can of fire-roasted corn instead, which added some richness and a hint of sweetness to go with the bell peppers. You have to give this a little time for the flavors to work together, and the pasta absorbs the dressing, which thickens it without drying it out. This one's going into the summer rotation and will be a go-to for pot-lucks - winner!

Loved the taste and change from traditional pasta salad. I love cumin so I used 1.5 tsp., I chopped in more fresh cilantro to taste and used a little more salsa as well. Great side dish with barbecues and can also stand on its own too. Have already recommended.

I really enjoyed this twist on pasta salad. Some people stated it was soupy, mine on the other hand was the opposite. After sitting overnight, it was kind of dry, so I mixed up some more dressing. I also doubled the spices and added more black beans. I switched the amounts of mayo and sour cream and I only had frozen corn and fresh cilantro. Will make again!

I made this for the first time and took it to a group potluck. It was a big hit. My family was delighted to get the leftovers. The only revision I made was to add about a cup and a half of shredded taco cheese. For lack of having them, the green onions were replaced with 1/3 cup sweet onion chopped fine. I will definitely be making this again and will experiment with the addition of chopped Roma tomatoes (seeded), more cheese, chopped jalapeno peppers, and more chunky salsa, plus more cumin and cilantro. Very good!!!
I doubled this recipe for a potluck. They almost licked the bowl clean. Awesome salad!!

Great recipe! Tips: 1/ add more diced red peppers if you want to make it more colourful and more importantly, for more texture in the salad); 2/ my salsa was really spicey so I just put in the ground pepper and not the cumin and it was perfect; 3/ don't put all the mayo and sour cream at once -put in half, stir your mixture and think about how creamy/fatty you want it, because I used the recomm'd amount and it was too creamy for my personal taste; 4/ ran out of olives, but it was still good--next time might throw in some tuna? I brought this to a southern bbq themed dinner and it went well with the corn bread and bbq chicken.

My son loves pasta salads, so I decided to try something new with a different twist. The only thing I did different was add 1 pound of ham bits/cubes. He's big on protein and it ended up being a really yummy addition.

It's excellent. Added in some chili powder, lime juice, and rehydrated an ancho Chili in the water while the pasta cooked, then emusified about half the ancho in the mayo/sour cream mixture for fun. Wouldve been great without it too. Good stuff
Sounds great and can't wait to try. Thinking a squeeze of lime and zest added would be good. Like another review mentioned some pepper jack cheese too.
I used vegan mayonnaise and sour cream instead of the animal products.

Thanks for all of the comments and suggestions.... I try to do a quick read thru, lots of help thanks.....good way to clean out a few things on the selves. I going to add my own grown red and green bell peppers
